results.corrected_title: Norwegian startup Sanna raises NOK 30 million for AI-driven accounting
results.corrected_summary: Sanna, a Norwegian accounting firm that does bookkeeping for a fixed price, has raised NOK 30 million in a round led by Skyfall Ventures and Alliance VC. That brings its total funding to NOK 44 million, and Dagens Næringsliv reports a NOK 120 million valuation. AI does much of the bookkeeping and authorised accountants check the results. Sanna says it has more than 2,000 customers in Norway and Sweden, mostly holding companies, and has recently opened the service to operating companies with employees.
key_facts: NOK 30m round led by Skyfall Ventures and Alliance VC; total raised NOK 44m
Valuation NOK 120m according to Dagens Næringsliv (cited by Shifter)
Other investors include existing investor Sondo and angels Eirik Rime (Tise), Fredrik Thomassen (Superside), Martin Schütt (Askeladden) and Lars Boilesen (former Opera CEO)
More than 2,000 customers in Norway and Sweden, mostly holding companies (the company's own figure)
Competitor: Visma-owned Mandora has launched Taki, an AI accountant for founders and micro-businesses
The money will go to technology development and hiring more authorised accountants
results.issues: None material. Only KI-pulsen calls it a 'seed' round. The customer count is the company's own claim. Shifter names Petter Reistad as founder.

results.corrected_title: NRK bans fully AI-generated songs from Melodi Grand Prix; Sweden's SVT does not
results.corrected_summary: NRK says 30 to 50 of the roughly 1,500 songs submitted for Melodi Grand Prix 2027 were made entirely by AI, even though such songs are banned. AI tools are still allowed in other parts of song production. Sweden's SVT received a record 4,077 entries for Melodifestivalen, suspects several are AI-generated, but will not introduce its own ban. The EBU has told NRK that entries should be based on human creativity, but there are no common guidelines for broadcasters yet.
key_facts: About 1,500 submissions to MGP 2027, of which 30 to 50 were made entirely by AI
MGP project leader Mads Tørklep: 'There's no point in having a music competition where a computer has done the whole job'
NRK's editorial team under music director Tarjei Strøm skips songs that are obviously AI-made; AI tools are allowed elsewhere in production
SVT: a record 4,077 Melodifestivalen entries, no ban, will follow the music industry (project leader Anders Wistbacka)
EBU email of 13 Oct 2026: AI must not replace human creativity, but there are no common ESC guidelines
results.issues: The original NRK story is dated 12 Oct 2026 (updated 13 Oct); Gaffa followed on 13 Oct. NRK says the ban was 'already introduced' but gives no date, so the ban itself may be older than this window. What is new in the window is the count of AI entries and the SVT/EBU comparison, so the story should be framed that way.

results.corrected_title: IMF: AI investment props up global growth; Georgieva warns of a 'slow-moving tsunami' for young workers
results.corrected_summary: In its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, released on 12 October around the IMF/World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, the IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% (from 3.0% in July) and kept 2027 at 3.4%. It credited strong AI investment and listed a downward reassessment of AI profitability and productivity expectations as a downside risk. Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said in Bangkok that AI's labour-market impact is a 'slow-moving tsunami' hitting young entry-level workers hardest; the IMF estimates about 40% of jobs worldwide will be affected. On 16 October, at an IMF conference in Bangkok, Fed chair Kevin Warsh called the AI spending surge a 'shock' and said the path ahead is likely to be 'a very bumpy one'.
key_facts: IMF October 2026 WEO: 2026 global growth 3.1% (up from 3.0% in July, 3.3% in January); 2027 3.4%, unchanged from July
AI investment named as a driver of the upgrade; a downward reassessment of AI profitability and productivity is a downside risk
Georgieva (12 Oct, Bangkok): AI disruption is a 'slow-moving tsunami', and young workers in routine entry-level jobs are most at risk
IMF estimate: about 40% of jobs worldwide will be augmented, downgraded or eliminated by AI
Fed chair Kevin Warsh (16 Oct, IMF conference in Bangkok): treat AI spending as a 'shock'; the path is likely 'a very bumpy one'
results.issues: The candidate dated the WEO 13 Oct, but SBS and the Reuters URL show it came out on 12 Oct. Georgieva's quote is 'slow-moving tsunami'. The ~40% figure is a long-standing IMF estimate, not new. The IMF's own report was not opened; the WEO numbers come from SBS and the Reuters search snippet.
